key_idea: Track the right profile of a partial 2-row filling: it is either flat or jagged by one cell; squares keep flat, S-tiles keep jagged, and a corner toggles between them.
sketch: Because every tile must fit in two rows, the frontier is flat or offset by exactly one cell. A square maps flat to flat, an S-tile maps jagged to jagged, and a corner switches state, so corners are used in pairs and S-tiles are only usable between a pair of corners (any number in one chain). Answer: 2a if c<2, else 2a + 2b + 3*floor(c/2) (each corner pair adds 3 columns, each S adds 2). O(1). Verified against an exhaustive tiling search for a,b<=2, c<=4. Pitfall: with c<2 the S-tiles are completely useless, and an odd corner is left over.
